# The Timeline API

:::note
This page is **specific to MotionScript 1.0.0**. The explicit `Timeline` object
was removed in later versions — animations are now driven directly by `yield*`
inside the scene generator, so there is no equivalent page in the current docs.
:::

In `1.0.0`, you could build an animation imperatively by pushing steps onto a
`Timeline` and playing it back, instead of (or alongside) `yield*`.

```tsx
import { makeScene, Rect, createRef, Timeline } from 'motion-script';

export default makeScene(function* (view) {
  const box = createRef<Rect>();
  view.add(<Rect ref={box} width={160} height={160} fill="royalblue" radius={12} />);

  const timeline = new Timeline();
  timeline.add(box().to({ x: 300 }, 1));
  timeline.add(box().to({ rotation: 180 }, 0.5));

  yield* timeline.play();
});
```

## Why it was removed

The `Timeline` object duplicated what `yield*` already expresses more directly,
and it made nested/parallel composition harder to reason about. From `2.0.0`
onward you compose flows with plain `yield*` and the `all`/`sequence` helpers:

```tsx
// Equivalent in newer versions — no Timeline needed:
yield* box().to({ x: 300 }, 1);
yield* box().to({ rotation: 180 }, 0.5);
```

If you are migrating off `1.0.0`, replace each `timeline.add(...)` /
`timeline.play()` with the corresponding `yield*` statements.
